{"filepath":"efficiency_analysis.md","content":"Efficiency analysis — normalized records and comparison to theoretical limits

Summary
- Ingested file: research_findings.json (records from company/institutional press releases and the NREL compilation).
- Normalization performed: numeric efficiencies unified to percent with two decimal places (where reported), device labeling standardized ("cell" vs "module"), test conditions (spectrum, concentration in suns, temperature) extracted and normalized where present.
- Caveats: dataset is a curated subset of research/company records. Several entries are company press releases that reference third-party certification (e.g., NREL) — primary-source certificates should be checked for formal verification before publication.

1) Normalized / validated records (table)
Note: values in the table are presented as normalized numeric efficiencies (percent). Device label is taken from device_type fields and standardized to "cell" or "module".

| id                  | date       | device_label | category (short)           | efficiency_pct | area_cm2 | spectrum / illumination | concentration_suns | temperature_C | certification (as stated)                                                                 | source_url |
|---------------------|------------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|----------|-------------------------|--------------------|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| fraunhofer-47.6-2022 | 2022-05-30 | cell         | multi-junction (concentrator) | 47.60%         | 0.5      | AM1.5D / direct-normal  | 665                | 25            | Measured and reported by Fraunhofer ISE (institutional measurement / press release).      | https://www.ise.fraunhofer.de/en/press-media/press-releases/2022/fraunhofer-ise-develops-the-worlds-most-efficient-solar-cell-with-47-comma-6-percent-efficiency.html |
| longi-33.9-2023     | 2023-11-03 | cell         | tandem (perovskite/silicon) | 33.90%         | 1.0      | AM1.5G                 | 1                  | 25            | Reported as verified/certified by NREL in company/press statements (LONGi / PR Newswire). | https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/longi-sets-a-new-world-record-of-33-9-for-the-efficiency-of-crystalline-silicon-perovskite-tandem-solar-cells-301978002.html |
| longi-34.6-2024     | 2024-06-14 | cell         | tandem (perovskite/silicon) | 34.60%         | 1.0      | AM1.5G                 | 1                  | 25            | Company press release (LONGi); independent lab certification not explicit in announcement. | https://www.longi.com/en/news/2024-snec-silicon-perovskite-tandem-solar-cells-new-world-efficiency |
| longi-34.85-2025    | 2025-04-16 | cell         | tandem (perovskite/silicon) | 34.85%         | 1.0      | AM1.5G                 | 1                  | 25            | Reported as certified by NREL in company announcement (LONGi).                             | https://www.longi.com/en/news/silicon-perovskite-tandem-solar-cells-new-world-efficiency |
| nrel-chart-2024     | 2024-05-02 | dataset      | compilation / dataset      | 47.60% (top listed) | n/a      | varied                 | varied             | varied        | NREL-curated compilation (interactive Best Research-Cell Efficiencies chart).            | https://www.nrel.gov/pv/cell-efficiency.html |

Notes on normalization and validation
- Efficiency values: numeric values were normalized to two decimal places and displayed with a percent sign (e.g., 34.85%). Where a source stated a value and a certification/verification (e.g., NREL) was mentioned in press text, that assertion was copied from the press text but should be confirmed against primary certification records.
- Device labeling: records containing the string "cell" in device_type were labeled as "cell". No records labeled "module" (commercial module) were present in the ingested JSON.
- Test conditions: spectrum and concentration are reported where available. Fraunhofer used concentrated illumination (665 suns, direct-normal). Longi entries use standard AM1.5G, 1 sun, 25 C conditions (typical research-cell test conditions).

2) (a) Current best reported efficiencies by category (based on ingested dataset)
- Lab single-junction (research cell, 1 sun): No explicit single-junction research-cell records are present in the ingested file. (The Shockley–Queisser single-junction limit of 33.7% is included in the dataset for comparison; see section 3.)

- Lab multi-junction (research cell / concentrator): Fraunhofer ISE — 47.60% (four-junction wafer-bonded concentrator cell, 665 suns, reported 2022). Source: Fraunhofer ISE press release. Link: https://www.ise.fraunhofer.de/en/press-media/press-releases/2022/fraunhofer-ise-develops-the-worlds-most-efficient-solar-cell-with-47-comma-6-percent-efficiency.html

- Commercial module (mass-produced modules): No commercial-module records are included in the ingested JSON. The dataset includes NREL compilation links that cover modules, but no explicit commercial-module entries were present in the file provided.

Other notable bests in the file
- Perovskite–silicon tandem research cells (lab): LONGi announcements showing progressive improvements: 33.90% (2023, reported with NREL verification claim), 34.60% (2024, SNEC announcement), 34.85% (2025, reported certified by NREL). Sources (LONGi):
  - 33.9% (2023): https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/longi-sets-a-new-world-record-of-33-9-for-the-efficiency-of-crystalline-silicon-perovskite-tandem-solar-cells-301978002.html
  - 34.6% (2024): https://www.longi.com/en/news/2024-snec-silicon-perovskite-tandem-solar-cells-new-world-efficiency
  - 34.85% (2025): https://www.longi.com/en/news/silicon-perovskite-tandem-solar-cells-new-world-efficiency

3) (b) Time-series summary (simple)
Normalized, chronological list of top records included in dataset (year — id — eff % — comment):
- 2022 — fraunhofer-47.6-2022 — 47.60% — four-junction concentrator cell, 665 suns (Fraunhofer ISE).
- 2023 — longi-33.9-2023 — 33.90% — silicon–perovskite tandem research cell (claimed NREL verification in press).
- 2024 — longi-34.6-2024 — 34.60% — incremental improvement announced at SNEC 2024 (company PR).
- 2024 — nrel-chart-2024 — top-listed 47.60% (NREL compilation listing Fraunhofer result among others).
- 2025 — longi-34.85-2025 — 34.85% — LONGi announcement citing NREL certification for tandem research cell.

Short textual chart descriptions (can be reproduced as small charts)
- Chart A (research-cell top efficiencies by year, 2022–2025): A simple line connecting 47.6% (2022) and then showing perovskite/silicon tandem series at ~33.9% (2023), 34.6% (2024), 34.85% (2025). This shows two separate threads: concentrator multi-junction devices at higher absolute efficiency (47.6%) and tandem/perovskite–silicon research cells climbing gradually in the mid-30% range.

- Chart B (efficiency vs test concentration): Two-point comparison: Fraunhofer 47.60% at 665 suns (concentrator) vs Longi 34.85% at 1 sun (AM1.5G). Description: When plotted with concentration on the x-axis (log scale) and efficiency on the y-axis, Fraunhofer sits at high concentration / high efficiency, while the tandem cells sit at 1 sun / mid-30% efficiency.

4) (c) Comparison to theoretical limits and contextual interpretation
Normalized theoretical limits included in the ingested dataset:
- Shockley–Queisser (single-junction SQ) limit: 33.7% (AM1.5G, 1 sun, ideal detailed-balance assumptions). Source references in dataset: LONGi press materials cite SQ = 33.7%.
- Ideal two-junction (perovskite/silicon tandem) detailed-balance limit (as cited in LONGi materials): ~43.0% (AM1.5G, 1 sun, idealized assumptions).
- High-concentration multi-junction contextual target: ~50% (aspirational/target figure referenced in Fraunhofer and other high-concentration programs); actual detailed-balance limits for many-junction cells under high concentration can exceed 50% depending on number of junctions.

Comparisons (measured vs limits)
- Longi 34.85% (perovskite–silicon tandem, 1 sun): Exceeds the single-junction SQ limit (33.7%) — as expected for a tandem device; remains below the cited two-junction ideal limit (43.0%) by ~8.15 percentage points (absolute). Interpretation: current record tandem cells are closing the gap but have substantial room to reach ideal two-junction limits, given real-world non-idealities (optical losses, non-radiative recombination, series resistance, suboptimal bandgap pairing, and interface losses).

- Fraunhofer 47.60% (four-junction concentrator, 665 suns): Exceeds the cited two-junction 43% limit (but note the two-junction limit is not applicable for a four-junction, highly concentrated device). Compared to the informal "~50%" aspirational target for high-concentration multi-junction devices, the Fraunhofer result is ~2.4 percentage points below that aspirational figure — a strong performance consistent with state-of-the-art concentrator multi-junction technology.

Important caveats when comparing records to theoretical limits
- The Shockley–Queisser (SQ) number and other detailed-balance limits assume ideal radiative recombination-limited behavior, perfect optics, and specific spectrum / concentration. Direct numerical comparison requires matching assumptions (number of junctions, bandgaps, spectrum, concentration). The dataset entries include mixed test conditions (1 sun AM1.5G vs high-concentration direct-normal), so comparisons must account for those differences.
- Certification status matters: some entries are company press releases that state independent verification; where the JSON notes a certification claim (e.g., NREL), check the relevant NREL certificate/entry or journal/independent lab report to confirm.

Appendix A — Small CSV of normalized records (for quick import)

"longi-34.6-2024",2024-06-14,cell,"tandem (perovskite/silicon)",34.60,1.0,"AM1.5G",1,25,"Company press release (independent lab certification not explicit)","https://www.longi.com/en/news/2024-snec-silicon-perovskite-tandem-solar-cells-new-world-efficiency"

"nrel-chart-2024",2024-05-02,dataset,"compilation / dataset",47.60,n/a,"varied","varied","varied","NREL Best Research-Cell Efficiencies compilation (dataset)","https://www.nrel.gov/pv/cell-efficiency.html"

Appendix B — Quick recommendations / next steps
- Verify certification claims by checking NREL records, published certification reports, or published peer-reviewed papers for the highlighted records (especially the Longi announcements that reference NREL verification/certification).
- If the broader mission is to estimate the practical "ceiling" for commercial modules, ingest additional curated data on commercial-module top records (independently certified module efficiencies from PV manufacturers and third-party labs) and the NREL module-efficiency table; normalize module test conditions (NOCT / STC) separately from lab-cell conditions.
- For more precise theoretical comparisons, compute bandgap-optimized detailed-balance limits for the specific number of junctions and the specific spectrum/concentration in each test condition (SQ for single-junction AM1.5G, two-junction detailed-balance for tandem, and high-concentration multi-junction detailed-balance for concentrators).

End of analysis

Prepared from research_findings.json (normalized and summarized)."}
